scores.evidence: 'Morning' section opens with 'If you only caught the last three laps' — narrative throat-clearing before any verdict
'Until next week' is a textbook wrap-up: standings summary, next-race tease, signed-off farewell
'At the time it looked like a routine split. It set up the rest of the afternoon.' — bridging sentence between sections, not heading-driven transition
'0.85s a lap… 31-second green-flag stop… 37 laps to recover… 25 left' — four figures clustered in the same analytical beat
'Would he have won anyway? I don't think so' and 'probably' absent but 'I don't think so' cleanly owns the speculation
Russell used as the explicit benchmark throughout: gap, tyre choice, VSC moment all benchmarked against team-mate before any absolute claim
Race control messages and stewards' bulletin quoted verbatim as hard stops: 'CAR 12 (ANT) TIME 1:28.582 DELETED – TRACK LIMITS AT TURN 1 LAP 49'
'Morning' section recaps the running order rather than interpreting it; 'If you only caught the last three laps, you saw the pass' is pure recap framing
'Same trick, one tyre step down' — flat juxtaposition; Gasly entry's deadpan 'The car drifted back to where its race pace put it'
'An Italian winning at Monza for the first time since 1966 is a line from the record books rather than from our data' — sentence is about the piece itself
No introductions, no definition of VSC or track-limits procedure; names and jargon deployed as peer shorthand throughout
Paragraphs consistently 2-4 sentences; 'Verstappen pitted at the same moment, took a hard, and got the same discount' exits cleanly on one point
'Half a second a lap quicker wasn't enough to get past at Monza. / This is the bit the 19th-to-first line hides' — long analytical then short punchy
VSC mechanism section gets proper room; but 'Morning' and 'About that grid penalty' absorb significant length on context rather than mechanism

top_fixes: Kill 'Until next week' entirely — the Winners/Losers: Noted:Pérez entry is the natural close; the standings paragraph and 'See you Sunday' are machine-newsletter habit and violate S2 outright.

Gut the 'Morning' section: it opens with a recap of what the reader saw and a record-books aside that the text itself flags as irrelevant — move the lap-3 point straight into 'The race was decided while it was stopped' and open that section on a verdict, not a sequence.

Tighten the number clusters in 'Take the VSC away': '0.85 a lap, 31-second stop, 37 laps, 25 left' lands as a calculation dump; give the arithmetic one figure (37 laps needed, 25 available) and let the conclusion carry the rest.
